svg.text: Splay Tree — Self-Adjusting BST with Amortized O(log n)
Splay Operation — Zig, Zig-Zig, Zig-Zag
• splay(x): rotate x to root using 3 cases
• Zig: x is child of root → single rotation
• Zig-Zig: x and parent same side → rotate parent first, then x
• Zig-Zag: x and parent opposite sides → rotate x twice
• After every access (find/insert/delete) → splay accessed node
• Recently accessed nodes stay near root → temporal locality
• No balance info stored — just BST pointers
BST Operations via Splay
• find(x): BST search → splay(x) if found, splay(predecessor) if not
• insert(x): BST insert → splay(x) → x becomes root
• delete(x): splay(x) → split into left/right subtrees
→ splay max of left subtree → attach right as its right child
• split(x): splay(x) → left subtree = keys < x, right = keys > x
• join(L, R): splay(max of L) → attach R as right child
• All ops amortized O(log n) — worst case O(n) per single op
Amortized Analysis — Potential Method
• Potential Φ = Σ rank(x) for all nodes x in tree
• rank(x) = floor(log₂(size of subtree rooted at x))
• Amortized cost of splay = O(rank(root) - rank(x)) + O(1)
• Since rank(root) = O(log n), each splay is O(log n) amortized
• Access Lemma: amortized cost ≤ 3(rank(t) - rank(x)) + 1
• Working Set Property: m ops on n items, item accessed t_i times
ago costs O(log t_i) — adapts to access frequency automatically
• Dynamic Finger: sequential access costs O(n) total → O(1) amortized
Variants & Real-World Applications
• vs AVL/Red-Black: no balance info → simpler node, better locality
• vs AVL/Red-Black: worst-case O(n) per op (ok if amortized suffices)
• Link-Cut Trees: splay trees on paths → dynamic tree connectivity
• GNU libstdc++ rope uses splay tree for string concatenation
• Cache simulation: LRU approximation via Working Set property
• Network routing: frequently accessed routes near root
• Conjecture (Sleator & Tarjan): splay trees are dynamically optimal
(unproven — one of the great open problems in data structures)
All ops: O(log n) amortized
Worst case: O(n) per op
Space: O(n) — no balance fields
3 rotation cases: Zig/Zig-Zig/Zig-Zag
Dynamic Optimality (conjectured)
